brief: Make EXTRA X tweets about Kaspa: more standalone Kaspa tweets than the default mix. No longform this batch.

fact_check.claim: 'The expectation was pretty damn bad and it's even worse than it was expected... we got the inflation reading' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified. September 2026 CPI (released Oct 14, 2026): +0.6% month over month (0.5% expected), 3.7% year over year (3.6% expected, 3.4% in August); core +0.3% on the month and 2.6% on the year, both above forecasts; gasoline +9.1% in the month. Copy uses 3.7%, 0.6%, 2.6%, 9.1% and 'hotter than expected'.

fact_check.claim: 'The odds of a rate hike only went up by a little bit... 34.4% today, yesterday it was 20... Polymarket traders put the odds of a 25 basis point hike on October 28th at 35% versus 66% for no change' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified and kept approximate. CME FedWatch after the CPI release: about 35% for a hike at the Oct 27-28 meeting, up from about 20-22% the day before (Yahoo 35%; Forbes 66% hold); CNBC quoted a higher 54% at one point in the day, so copy says 'about one in three' / 'from about 20% to about 35%' and never a decimal. A hike by December is priced above 96% (CNBC), written as 'better than 95%'. The Fed hiked on Sept 16, 2026 to 3.75% to 4.00%, its first hike in three years. The Polymarket 35/66 split could not be re-fetched and is not quoted as Polymarket; it matches the CME figure.

fact_check.claim: 'The five year yield just hit a new 19 year high at 5.15%, 115 basis points above the Fed's rate of 3.75 to 4.0... highest rate to borrow for five years since 2007' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified in direction, figure NOT used. The 5-year yield rose about 15 bp on Oct 14 to its highest level since 2007; a curve tracker showed 5.05% that day and the 10-year about 5.2-5.3%. The exact 5.15% could not be confirmed (intraday vs close), so copy says 'above 5% for the first time since 2007' and '10-year above 5.2%'.

fact_check.claim: 'One trillion wiped out from the US stock market today'; 'stocks dumping and crypto really isn't' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: CORRECTED. No source reports a $1 trillion wipeout on Oct 14; the S&P 500 closed down about 1.1% and the Nasdaq about 1.9%, with the Dow flat. Copy says 'stocks dropped only about 1% on the print' and never the trillion figure.

fact_check.claim: 'US Treasury to buy back six billion in long term debt tomorrow... maybe everybody's being psyched about some QE' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified as a program (Treasury has been running up-to-$6B buybacks of long-dated debt since September), but the specific date is day-relative and the QE read is speculation, so it is NOT used in any copy.

fact_check.claim: 'Bitcoin is 81, the 50 week moving average is at 77, only like a 4k drop... a channel is forming... people front running the October bottom pushed us above the May high in September... they pushed us below the 50 week moving average last November' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified and UPDATED. $BTC $81,413 (CoinGecko, -1.9% 7d, +3.9% 30d, ATH $126,080 on Oct 6, 2025). 50-week SMA from the last 50 completed weekly Coinbase closes is about $77.1K, so 'about $4K below at roughly $77K' holds. Coinbase daily candles: 2026 low $57,718 on July 1; May 2026 high $82,814; September high $87,397; October low so far $80,315. Bitcoin traded below its 50-week SMA from October 2025 (Leverage Shares, Dec 2025) and reclaimed it in September 2026 (archie-promo plan, Sept 20 breakout), so 'sold below the 50-week SMA last November, pushed back above in September' is kept general. '50 week moving average' written as 50-week SMA.

fact_check.claim: 'Kaspa, 3.6 cents right now... down at its lowest level for the week but it's still up for the month... another great buy... everything worthy of buying is worthy of a DCA at this particular moment' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified and UPDATED. $KAS $0.03664 (about 3.7 cents), about a $1.02B cap, rank 76, -5.7% 24h, -8.3% 7d, -14.7% 14d, +4.9% 30d; ATH $0.2074 on July 31, 2024, so about 82% under it. Copy uses 'about 3.7 cents', 'lowest level of the week', 'still up on the month', 'about 82% under its all-time high of 20.7 cents', 'about a $1B market cap'. 'Another great buy' and the DCA stance are Mike's own. Fair launch / no premine / proof of work are persona core theses; no TPS figure is used.

fact_check.claim: 'TAO going to 3000? Hell yeah, I totally agree. I think TAO can go a lot more than that in the long run... we should be going into one hell of a fantastic economic expansion' (transcript, Whisper 'Tao')
fact_check.verdict: verified and UPDATED. $TAO $268.84, about a $3.05B cap, rank 36, -6.6% 7d, +15.8% 30d; ATH $757.60 on March 7, 2024, so about 64% under it; $3,000 / $269 = about 11.2x, written 'roughly an 11x from here'. The $3,000 target is a viewer's number that Mike endorsed on stream, written as his own conviction. Whisper's Greek-letter mishear corrected to TAO everywhere. persona project_handles tao = null, so no Follow line. The bittensor-tao.png reference is cited on the image.

fact_check.claim: 'Some of those decent memes that have been around... Toshi, Turbo, Pengu, definitely Pengu... some won't make their all time highs but you can sort of be assured that they're going to pump and give you like a 10x' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified and UPDATED with the guarantee softened. $PENGU $0.00758, about a $477M cap, rank 119, -11.3% 7d, +7.1% 30d; ATH $0.0684 on Dec 17, 2024, so about 89% under it and about 9x to the old high. Copy never says 'assured'; it says the established memes with real exchange listings 'are the ones that come back when meme season returns' and 'its old high from here is about a 9x'. Follow: @pudgypenguins per project_handles. Turbo ($63M cap) and Toshi ($44M) were covered in the aliens batch (2026-10-09) and are not repeated. No Pudgy Penguins reference image exists, so the image is entity-free (see missing_references).

fact_check.claim: 'Mr. TA himself, the king of the four year cycle zombies, Benjamin Cowen, was absolutely perplexed about how Bitcoin went above the May high... people are front running the October bottom because they realize the bottom is in' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified in substance, 'perplexed' NOT attributed to him as a quote. Cowen's late-May 2026 cycle model (Bitcoin near $75.6K at the time) called a Q4 2026 bottom with October the most likely month, based on the last top falling inside the day count of the two prior cycles. On Sept 25, 2026 he posted that the weekly close would set up Q4 and that 'If Bitcoin accepts above the May high, that will improve the bull case substantially', with acceptance back below 'a massive fakeout before typical Q4 weakness'. Copy quotes only those words, describes him as 'staring at a chart that broke his model' (Mike's characterisation, in Mike's voice) and keeps 'I was not perplexed' in first person. The front-running read and the self-defeating October bottom are persona core_theses item 9, drafted per its rule (the zombies' demand is why the bottom never lands in October; never that they cause an October bottom). Benjamin-Cowen.png is used as the V4 topic photo.

fact_check.claim: 'If this war never started, or if it was concluded within the six weeks... none of this inflation stuff would have happened... Trump decides he wants to attack Iran, you can't predict that on a chart' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: kept GENERAL. The specific war claim is a political/geopolitical tangent (persona avoid_in_drafts) and its causal chain is not independently verified, so copy says 'you cannot chart an inflation shock' and anchors on the verified gasoline +9.1% / CPI 3.7% figures. No country, leader or war is named.

fact_check.claim: 'Golden Kitty is doing better than most, even though it's essentially dead too... went over 400k again... to be at 285... I saw his new token and I would stay away... the dev took the liquidity out?' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified (Golden Kitty about $295K-$312K cap on DexScreener, down 9-16% on the day) but NOT drafted: Mike's Golden Kitty exit already shipped (golden-kitty and grapes batches), the 'liquidity pulled' claim is a viewer comment he could not confirm, and the promoter's new 'Hellhound' token could not be verified, so nothing is built on it.

fact_check.claim: 'I also bought some ARB... it's the tech behind Robinhood... tokenized stock narrative'; 'there's a new one in my group for my members... VCs, tens of millions in funding' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified (Robinhood Chain is an Arbitrum Orbit L2; $ARB $0.18, +35% 30d) but NOT drafted: a 'what I bought this week' tweet is trader-portfolio framing (persona no_rotation_framing) and the members-only pick is a membership pitch.

fact_check.claim: 'Meme coin dominance is falling off a cliff' (transcript); 'a spawn? I never sold my spawn'; 'Holly Marcus said 80% chance the Clarity Act passes'; 'Ramses up 125%'; Stonk, Pons, Kitsu, YOLO, Vault, Veil, Flame, Rage Guy, Nauts, Polly, Candle, Broker Cat (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: meme dominance verified (about 3% of the altcoin market, CryptoQuant Oct 5, 2026) and used only as one supporting line in an IG caption because the full thesis shipped in the aliens batch. 'spawn' is the SPON mishear (persona spon_not_spawn); SPON is a position Mike is down on with no news, not drafted. The Clarity Act odds are a viewer's number, not drafted. None of the small Robinhood-chain / launchpad tokens are drafted (unverified caps, dead charts, no references).
no 'Zcash' or 'ZEC' string appears in this transcript; nothing to resolve.

fact_check.claim: PPI timing: 'at 8:30 tomorrow morning Eastern time' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: day-relative and stale by post time; copy says 'PPI is next' with no date.

ig_single.hook: The four-year cycle zombies are still waiting for the October bottom.
ig_single.caption:
The four-year cycle zombies are still waiting for the October bottom.

Bitcoin's ($BTC) low this year printed on July 1 at about $57.7K. Then the front-runners piled in through September, took it above the May high to about $87K, and now the zombies get to buy their 'October dip' at about $81K, from the people who bought the summer.

That is the whole joke of the October bottom: because the zombies, and the people front-running them, all plan to buy in October, the actual low prints BEFORE October. Their own demand is the reason the bottom never lands in October.

Kaspa Maxis did not wait for a calendar. We stacked $KAS through the summer and we are still adding at about 3.7 cents, lowest level of the week and still up on the month.

How am I wrong? Tell me in the comments.

ig_single.caption:
The divider between a dead token and a sleeping one is whether the team still posts every day.

I scrolled a graveyard of charts on stream this week: token after token down 90% or more, and the only ones with a pulse were the ones where the team refuses to quit, posting every few hours into the silence. When the pumps come back, those are the ones that come back to life. The rest stay dead.

Kaspa ($KAS) never has that problem. No team to quit, no premine to dump, no company whose budget runs out. Proof-of-work miners keep the chain running at 3.7 cents exactly the same as at 20 cents, block after block, whether anyone is posting about it or not. That is what a fair launch buys you in a dead market: a chain that does not need a cheerleader to survive.
